welcome.title: Welcome, Explorer!
welcome.pari_tip: There are no wrong ideas in this workbook. Try your best, ask questions, and have fun learning about AI!

syllabus.objective: I can map real AI use cases to domains and data types.
I can classify data and identify data quality problems.
I can calculate probability and compare the spread of data.
I can use dictionaries and basic pandas operations.
I can compute a perceptron's output and explain activation.
I can perform a simple convolution and explain CNN features.
I can write structured prompts and use generative AI
I can explain consent, copyright and deepfake risks.

units.title: AI Domains in Action
learn_paragraphs:
AI is used across sectors: healthcare (scan analysis), agriculture (pest detection),
finance (fraud detection), education (adaptive learning) and governance (service
delivery).
Each use belongs to a domain: Data Science, Computer Vision or NLP, and many
combine two or more.
Choosing the right domain depends on the type of data: numbers, images or
language.

new_words.definition: a value added to shift the output
how sure a model is about its answer

units.did_you_know: India's UPI handles billions of payments every month, and banks use AI to spot suspicious transactions.
units.think_and_talk: Which sector in India could benefit most from AI? Justify your answer.

units.title: Data Literacy
learn_paragraphs:
Structured data fits in rows and columns (marks, prices). Unstructured data does
not (images, audio, free text).
Data quality has dimensions: accuracy, completeness, consistency and timeliness.
Data cleaning fixes missing values, duplicates and wrong formats before training.

units.title: Statistics and Probability
learn_paragraphs:
Probability measures how likely something is: P = favourable outcomes ÷ total
outcomes, between 0 and 1.
Standard deviation shows how spread out data is. Low = values close together; high
= spread out.
AI models often output probabilities, like “87% chance this is a cat”.

new_words.definition: AI-made fake media of a real person

units.did_you_know: A weather forecast of 70% chance of rain means rain is expected on about 7 of 10 similar days.
units.think_and_talk: An AI says “60% chance this X-ray shows disease”. What should a doctor do?
units.self_check: I can calculate probability and compare the spread of data.

units.title: Python for Data
learn_paragraphs:
Dictionaries store key–value pairs: {"name": "Asha", "marks": 88} .
The pandas library loads tables as a DataFrame and makes analysis easy.
Common steps: read_csv() to load, head() to preview, mean() to summarise, and
filters to select rows.
units.did_you_know: pandas is free and open source, and is used by data scientists worldwide.
units.think_and_talk: Why do data scientists use libraries instead of writing everything from scratch?
units.self_check: I can use dictionaries and basic pandas operations.

units.title: Neural Networks in Depth
learn_paragraphs:
A perceptron computes a weighted sum plus a bias, then applies an activation
function.
z = w1·x1 + w2·x2 + b. A step activation outputs 1 if z ≥ 0, else 0. Modern networks
use functions like ReLU = max(0, z).
Training uses the error to adjust weights a little at a time, repeated over many
examples.

new_words.definition: a confident but false AI answer
a small grid of numbers used as a filter

units.did_you_know: The perceptron was invented by Frank Rosenblatt in 1958.
units.think_and_talk: How is an artificial neuron similar to, and different from, a brain neuron?

units.title: Convolution and Image Features
learn_paragraphs:
A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) finds features in images using small grids
called filters or kernels.
The filter slides over the image. At each spot we multiply matching numbers and add
them: this is convolution.
Early layers find edges; deeper layers find shapes like eyes or wheels.

units.title: Generative AI and Prompting
learn_paragraphs:
Generative AI creates new text, images, audio or code. Large Language Models
(LLMs) predict the next token using patterns from huge text data.
LLMs can hallucinate: give confident but false answers. Always verify facts.
Good prompts give a role, task, context, constraints and output format.

units.did_you_know: LLMs don't look up facts like a search engine unless they are connected to a search tool.

units.title: AI Ethics and Law
learn_paragraphs:
India's Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023 gives people rights over
their personal data and requires consent for most uses.
Copyright protects creative work. Using others' work to train or generate content
raises legal questions.
Deepfakes can harm reputations and spread misinformation. Responsible AI needs
transparency, consent and accountability.
